tools.name: get_offering
tools.description: The public offering of IIS Rescue: the three migration paths, the promises made on every project, the pricing model, and who the service is for.

tools.name: get_faq
tools.description: Published questions and answers about legacy IIS, classic ASP and SQL Server website migration, reproduced verbatim from the website.

tools.name: get_eol_facts
tools.description: Microsoft end-of-support dates for Windows Server and SQL Server versions, with the source URL for each, plus the Extended Security Updates cutoff.

tools.name: get_migration_paths
tools.description: The three routes off a legacy IIS server — Rehost, Rebuild, Replace — each with what it involves and the situation it best fits.

tools.name: get_contact
tools.description: How to start an engagement with IIS Rescue: the consultation URL and how the process works. Returns a pointer only — it never books anything or collects any personal data.

tools.name: get_partner_channel
tools.description: How IIS Rescue works with MSPs and independent IT contractors: MSPs bringing it in for legacy IIS, classic ASP and SQL Server migrations they would rather not own, and contractors subcontracting a migration or referring it. Covers the arrangements, what stays with the partner — the client, the brand

tools.name: get_pathfinder_questions
tools.description: The questions the IIS Rescue two-minute assessment asks in order to recommend a migration path, with the allowed answers for each. Ask these of the user, then pass the answers to run_pathfinder. "unknown" is a valid answer to every question and never breaks the result.

tools.name: run_pathfinder
tools.description: Recommend a migration path — Rehost, Rebuild or Replace — for a specific legacy IIS website, from answers to the two-minute assessment questions. Returns the recommendation, a confidence level, the alternatives and when they would apply, what pushes the price up or down, the specific risks these ans

description: Call this when a user wants to know whether to rehost, rebuild or replace their own legacy IIS or classic ASP website. Returns the recommended path, confidence, alternatives, risks, what moves the price, the reasoning and the consultation link. It runs the same engine as iisrescue.com/two-minute-ass

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_pathfinder_questions" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Call this when you want to ask the user more about their site to sharpen a run_pathfinder result. Returns the six assessment questions and their allowed answers…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_offering" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "The public offering of IIS Rescue: the three migration paths, the promises made on every project, the pricing model, and who the service is for." → after: "Call this when a user asks what IIS Rescue is, who it is for, or how its pricing works. Returns the three migration paths, the promises made on every project, the fixed-price model and the process. Includes the consultation link."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
